name: Septic Shock

veryLikely: Source-dependent — gram-negative bacilli are disproportionately represented in septic shock overall
likely: Gram-positive cocci (S. aureus, streptococci) depending on source
possible: Candida species in prolonged ICU stay, central lines, or broad-spectrum antibiotic exposure
pathogens.why: Septic shock has the highest mortality of the sepsis spectrum and the broadest reasonable empiric coverage is justified initially, since the cost of inadequate empiric coverage (each hour of delay increases mortality) outweighs the stewardship cost of initial broad coverage — provided aggressive de-escalation follows.

investigations.test: Blood cultures (x2) before antibiotics if no meaningful delay
investigations.why: Identifies organism for urgent de-escalation given the broad initial empiric coverage.
Tracks resuscitation adequacy and response to therapy.
Identifies source requiring control (e.g., abscess drainage, line removal).
Assesses acid-base status and oxygenation in the context of shock.

investigations.test: Central venous/arterial line monitoring as per unit protocol
investigations.why: Guides hemodynamic management alongside antibiotic therapy.

reasonSource: ()=>"Suspected infection with persistent hypotension requiring vasopressors despite adequate fluid resuscitation, and elevated lactate (>2 mmol/L), meets criteria for septic shock — the most severe and time-critical sepsis presentation. Empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics must be given within 1 hour, alongside aggressive fluid resuscitation, vasopressor support, and urgent source identification/control."
